title: NCAA Waiver Lets Coit Shine in Second KU Season
text:
David Coit,a guard for⁤ the Kansas⁢ Jayhawks,has gained​ meaningful attention due to a ‍new JUCO eligibility waiver that ​could extend his college basketball career. Here’s a thorough overview of his⁢ situation:
Eligibility Waiver : Coit was ‍granted ​an eligibility waiver by⁢ the NCAA⁤ on July ​18, ​2024. This ⁣waiver allows⁣ him to ⁣play‌ an ‍additional​ year of college basketball, despite having already played‍ at a junior college and‍ another institution. This is due to an ⁤administrative error in ⁢documenting his time at⁤ a post-graduate prep school, Scotland campus (Source: [2]). College ​Career : ​Coit played one year at Atlantic⁢ Cape Community College, were he averaged⁤ 30.6 points per game, leading the nation in scoring at the⁢ NJCAA division level. He then spent two years⁢ at Northern‌ Illinois before ⁣transferring to⁤ Kansas (Source: [2]). Impact ⁣of the Waiver : The waiver has opened up opportunities for Coit ⁤to play a fifth‍ year of college basketball. Kansas⁢ coach Bill Self⁢ acknowledged the possibility ⁣of ​Coit playing another year⁤ on December 30, ​2024 (Source: [1]). NCAA’s Blanket Waiver : The NCAA’s ⁤blanket waiver,which Coit benefited from,was issued shortly after Vanderbilt quarterback Diego Pavia earned an injunction​ to play another year of football. This waiver has⁤ been litigated and re-litigated, but Coit’s case is considered clear-cut as he began his​ college career at a junior college (Source: [3]). Potential Benefits : Coit believes that an additional year of college basketball could⁢ help him both on and off the⁢ court ‌(Source: [3]). David Coit’s eligibility waiver has provided ⁤him with an opportunity to ​extend his college basketball career, and his case is seen as a clear-cut example of the NCAA’s blanket waiver in action.
After NCAA’s Blanket Waiver, Coit Eager to‌ Spend Second Season at KU In a recent growth, the NCAA’s blanket waiver has paved the way for ​numerous student-athletes to​ extend their collegiate⁢ careers, ‍and among them is‌ Jalen Coit , a standout ‍guard for the university of Kansas (KU) Jayhawks. Coit,who has been a vital bench player this season,expressed his enthusiasm‍ and gratitude‌ for the opportunity to continue his journey at KU.
“I think it’s a blessing,” Coit said. “I⁢ think​ it’s going to be fun, but⁣ got to be where my⁢ feet are at, and just focus on one day at a​ time,‌ and then obviously use that extra year to my advantage, get‌ my⁤ master’s ⁤and ‍different things ​like that.”
A Key piece ​for the​ Jayhawks The 5-foot-11 guard has made significant contributions ⁢to the Jayhawks this season, especially‌ on ‍the defensive ⁣end. Despite ⁣facing a shooting slump ​throughout much of January, Coit ⁤has remained a consistent presence on the ‍court. He ⁤has played in every game⁤ for KU, averaging 15 minutes off the bench with 4.5 points per​ game‍ and a 37.1% shooting percentage from ‌beyond the arc.
Utilizing the Extra Year The additional⁣ year ⁤of eligibility ‌granted by the NCAA’s blanket waiver presents a unique‌ opportunity for Coit. Not only will he get to continue his basketball career, but ⁣he will‍ also have ‍the chance to pursue academic goals, such as obtaining ​a master’s degree. This dual benefit is something ⁣Coit is eager to capitalize on.
“I think it’s a blessing,” Coit​ reiterated.“I ⁤think⁢ it’s going ​to be fun, but‍ got to ⁤be where my ⁣feet are at, ⁤and⁣ just focus on one day at a time, and then obviously use⁤ that extra year⁤ to my advantage, get my master’s and different things ⁣like that.”
Looking Ahead As ⁣coit ⁤and the⁣ Jayhawks prepare for the ‍upcoming challenges,the⁤ guard’s focus remains on the present. He understands the ⁣importance⁤ of⁤ taking things one day at a‌ time and making the most of⁢ each opportunity that ⁤comes his way.
